etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English gaspen, gayspen (“to gape, outbreathe”), related to and likely derived from Old Norse geispa (“to yawn”) or its descendant Danish gispe, which may be related to gapa (“to gape”).

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To draw in the breath suddenly, as if from a shock.
(intransitive) To breathe quickly or in a labored manner, as after exertion; to respire with heaving of the breast; to pant.

quote.citation: c. 1761-1764, Robert Lloyd, An Epistle to C. Churchill, Author of the Rosicad
quote.text: She gasps and struggles hard for life.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To speak in a breathless manner.
To pant with eagerness or excitement; to show vehement desire.

quote.citation: 1579, Immeritô [pseudonym; Edmund Spenser], “Aprill. Aegloga Quarta.”, in The Shepheardes Calender: […], London:  […]  Iohn Wolfe for Iohn Harrison the yonger, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Quenching the gasping furrows' thirst with rain.

definitions.definition: A short, sudden intake of breath.
(British, slang): A draw or drag on a cigarette (or gasper).
